chunks: Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Abi Ja'far al-Bayhaqi in Fayd, after my return from the pilgrimage to the House of Allah the Exalted in the year 354 A.H., narrated to us: Ali ibn Ja'far al-Madani narrated to us: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated to me: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (Ali ibn al-Husayn), from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When the Day of Resurrection comes, we will be in charge of the reckoning of our followers. Whoever has a grievance between him and Allah the Exalted, we will judge in it and He will endorse our judgment. Whoever has a grievance between him and the people, we will ask them to forgive him, and they will forgive on our behalf. And whoever has a grievance between him and us, we are more deserving to pardon and overlook than anyone else.

key_terms.اسْتَوْهَبْنَاهَا: we asked for forgiveness on their behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the Imams in judging the sins of their followers on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the progeny of Imam al-Rida (a.s.), establishes the Imams as intercessors and judges on the Day of Resurrection, reflecting the Shia doctrine of their spiritual authority over the faithful. It categorizes accountability into three tiers: personal sins against God are judged by the Imams with divine approval, interpersonal debts are resolved through the Imam's intercession to secure human forgiveness, and grievances against the Imams themselves are waived due to their precedence in mercy. This hierarchy underscores the Imams' role not just as guides, but as active mediators who facilitate the believer's entry into Paradise by settling both divine and social accounts.
